apiContracts: Every endpoint requires author(u), which accepts an authenticated author or administrator session.

Creator records and story projections are scoped to the authenticated session owner u.id. Administrator role does not permit reading another creator's private goals, notes, analytics or feedback through these workspace endpoints.

Analytics returns a bounded top-100 novel list and top-10 chapter list, while lifetime totals are calculated separately across all novels owned by u.id; Crown spend is reader spending, not author earnings or payout balance.
Feedback returns only ratings and visible comments attached to novels owned by u.id; rating identities are represented as Reader.
Story goals are unique per novel and may be cleared by setting all targets and target date empty. Target counts and date values are bounded and validated.

Private notes are limited to 4,000 characters, can optionally target a chapter belonging to the selected owned novel, and all reads/updates/deletes require owner_user_id=u.id plus current parent ownership.
Readiness and planning projections are read-only and bounded to 100 owned novels/items. Planning excludes drafts that already have a scheduled publication.
Private note chapter metadata is joined through both chapter ID and the note's parent novel ID so a malformed cross-novel reference cannot expose another story's chapter title.
Story goal date parsing rejects invalid calendar values with a 400 validation response and must not throw on out-of-range month/day inputs.
Creator Studio receives the platform audit callback through Worker dependency injection; it must not reference an undeclared global audit function.
dataEntities: Reuses novels, chapters, ratings, comments, chapter_views and unlocks.
Reuses author_story_goals from migration 0032 and author_private_notes from migration 0033.
Migration 0047 rebuilds author_story_goals with a composite (owner_user_id,novel_id) primary key, preserving each former owner's private goal while allowing the current owner a separate row.

migrationPlan.canonicalEntityReuse: Migration 0032 remains immutable. Migration 0047 rebuilds the existing goals table with a composite owner/novel key and preserves all existing rows; no parallel goals table is introduced.
migrationPlan.backwardCompatibility: Existing goal rows and values are copied unchanged. Creator API upserts now target (owner_user_id,novel_id), so ownership transfer does not expose or overwrite a former creator's private goal.
migrationPlan.rollbackOrForwardRepair: Migration history is append-only. If code rollback is needed, retain the composite schema and restore compatible owner+novel upsert behavior; do not attempt to reintroduce novel_id-only uniqueness.

uiLifecycle.ssrBehavior: No SSR route changes in this slice.
uiLifecycle.clientBootBehavior: Existing Author Studio shell consumes the authenticated Creator workspace APIs; no duplicate browser boot owner is introduced.
uiLifecycle.servedBundleParity: No new browser asset is introduced by the Creator API module.

privacySecurity.authentication: Requires authenticated author or administrator session through author(u).
privacySecurity.authorization: Every route checks author(u); data access is constrained to the authenticated owner rather than administrator impersonation.
privacySecurity.ownerScoping: All creator-facing story queries and note mutations bind owner_user_id to u.id and recheck parent novel ownership.
privacySecurity.csrf: Existing Worker origin and session protections remain in force.
privacySecurity.rateAndSizeLimits: Private notes max 4,000 characters; analytics, feedback, readiness and planning reads are bounded.
privacySecurity.rightsAndPrivacy: Analytics and feedback are scoped to the creator's owned stories. No public endpoint or chapter-body ingestion is added.
privacySecurity.audit: All creator-goal mutations invoke the injected platform audit callback; audit persistence remains centralized in the Worker.

unit: test-creator-publishing-domain-boundaries.mjs validates Creator/Publishing ownership boundaries and owner-scope source predicates.
test-api-route-method-matrix.mjs verifies route source line evidence and feature module Git blob fingerprints.
test-ownership-transfer-migration.mjs validates migration 0047 preserves the former creator's private goal and permits a separate goal row for the new owner.
integration: test-worker-account-reader-isolation.mjs verifies two-account Worker/D1 isolation for all Creator Studio route-methods, including analytics, feedback, goals, private notes CRUD, readiness and planning.
The same local Worker/D1 test verifies Publishing release calendar, revision privacy, schedule create/cancel and ownership-transfer cancellation.
The two-account Worker/D1 test transfers a novel after the former owner creates a goal, then verifies the new owner can create and read a separate goal while the former owner cannot read it.
isolation: Author A must not read or mutate Author B goals or private notes, nor view Author B analytics, feedback, readiness or planning results.
Author A and B cannot read or mutate each other's Creator Studio records or Publishing release records.
A former owner cannot cancel a schedule after ownership changes; the current owner can.

stagingSteps: Run exact-head architecture, route, schema parity, Graphify and Cloudflare validation.
Run two-account Worker/D1 tests before marking the Creator routes authorization-reviewed.
Verify analytics totals across more than 100 owned novels and ensure the top-100 display cap does not cap totals.

rollback.codeRollback: Revert Creator Studio module dispatch and module together; retain existing canonical creator application and AI routes.
rollback.dataRollbackOrForwardRepair: No migration or data mutation is required for rollback.

collisionReview.duplicateRoutes: No duplicate Creator routes are intended; the release calendar and chapter lifecycle routes are Publishing-owned.
collisionReview.duplicateEntities: No duplicate goals, notes, chapter or account entities are introduced.
collisionReview.migrationAllocation: Migrations 0032 and 0033 are reused; no new migration.
collisionReview.sharedSurfaceOwners: creator owns workspace behavior; platform-kernel owns Worker dispatch; platform-data owns existing persistence; platform-quality owns tests; platform-architecture owns route and authorization inventories; platform-integrator serializes shared changes.

changeSummary: Defines the Creator-owned editorial workspace boundary for analytics, reader feedback, writing goals, private notes, editorial readiness and planning. Lifetime analytics totals are independent of the top-100 display list. Existing goals and notes migrations are reused. Correct the story-goal upsert target column order so authenticated owner IDs and novel IDs are persisted in their respective columns. Creator Studio audit logging is explicitly injected by the Worker composition, preventing undefined audit callback failures after writes.
acceptanceCriteria: All Creator routes are present in the API method inventory with module source evidence.
All creator-facing reads and mutations are scoped to session u.id; admin role does not enable cross-owner access.
Lifetime analytics totals cover every owned novel, independent of the top-100 list.
Private note mutations verify both note owner and current parent novel owner.
Existing author applications, AI projects and publishing routes remain available.
New Creator endpoints remain authorization-pending until two-account Worker/D1 tests pass.
After ownership transfer, the former creator cannot read the old private goal and the new owner can create a separate goal for the same novel.
Migration 0047 is reserved to PR #294, preserves existing goal rows, and is validated by the ownership-transfer migration test.
